assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political economics gave a unified, rigorous framework for how electoral rules, constitutions, and state capacity shape fiscal policy and growth. It has changed both theory and empirical practice in public economics, comparative politics, and development, and it follows the 2024 institutions prize in subject matter without duplicating it.
assessment.attribution: The core contributions are the Persson–Tabellini work on constitutions and policy outcomes and the Besley–Persson work on state capacity. A trio is natural, and the credit is comparatively clean and well documented.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of cumulative work, with canonical books and many validated empirical applications. Timing is not a constraint.
uncertainties: Persson is at IIES, my home institute, and I disclose this as a potential conflict without adjudicating it.
The committee may judge that the 2024 institutions prize and earlier public choice and political economy awards have already covered much of this ground.
Besley's inclusion versus a two-person award is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the trade-shock evidence reshaped how economists understand labour demand, wage inequality, and the distributional costs of technology and globalisation. The work combines conceptual models with credible identification, and it has had large policy influence.
assessment.attribution: Katz and Autor lead the skill-biased and task-based technological change line. Autor, Dorn, and Hanson lead the China-shock evidence. The three names selected cover the main arcs, but the tasks framework also has major contributors outside this entry.
assessment.maturity: Work from the 1990s to the 2010s, widely replicated and refined, with durable influence across labour, trade, and macro.
uncertainties: The task-model lineage has important contributors not in the credited set, which complicates attribution.
My own work on capital-skill complementarity is closely related, so I disclose a field proximity.
The long-run welfare interpretation of the China shock is still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-firm trade models changed the field's core framework by explaining selection, exporter premia, and new gains from trade through reallocation. They are now the workhorse of both theory and quantitative trade and have transformed empirical work on firm-level data.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution, and Helpman's broader program on trade with differentiated products and firm heterogeneity is the other major strand. Redding is important for quantification but is the less central of the three.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of consolidation and extension, with extensive empirical validation using micro data.
uncertainties: Krugman's 2008 prize partly covers the monopolistic-competition foundation, so some committee members may see this as incremental.
Credit overlaps with the quantitative trade entry and with Helpman's work on trade politics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities is the dominant paradigm for monetary policy analysis in central banks. It gives a micro-founded account of how policy rules and expectations determine inflation and output.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread widely: Calvo for staggered pricing, Taylor for rules, Woodford and Galí for the canonical synthesis, and Christiano–Eichenbaum–Evans, Smets–Wouters, and Gertler for medium-scale estimation. Any three-person selection leaves out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and thoroughly tested, including through the post-2008 and 2021–22 inflation episodes. That testing has raised new questions but has not displaced the framework.
uncertainties: The three-laureate cap forces a contested choice among at least eight credited names.
Recent inflation episodes and the heterogeneous-agent critique may temper enthusiasm for the representative-agent version.
Prior prizes in monetary and macro theory (Lucas, Sargent–Sims, Kydland–Prescott) overlap partly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Granular household-level evidence showed how credit expansion, household leverage, and balance-sheet shocks drive booms, busts, and the depth of recessions. This reoriented post-2008 macro-finance and links to the heterogeneous-agent macro literature.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the clear leaders, with a coherent body of joint work and a book. Campbell's contributions to household finance and asset pricing are valuable but peripheral to this specific discovery.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from about 2009–2018 and have been replicated across countries. This is mature enough for consideration, but the debate on mechanisms is not settled.
uncertainties: Some results, such as the causal role of credit supply versus demand, have been contested.
The line is comparatively recent next to other candidates, and may be better judged in a few years.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework quantifies how distortions in the allocation of inputs across firms account for large cross-country income gaps. It joins micro-data with aggregate theory, and it has reshaped development accounting and growth empirics.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh–Klenow (2009) is the pivotal paper. Restuccia–Rogerson (2008) is an equally important parallel contribution, and its authors are not both in the credited set, which makes the attribution contestable.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of use, with large follow-up literatures. The measurement approach has also drawn criticism about sensitivity to measurement error and model assumptions.
uncertainties: Parallel authorship (Restuccia–Rogerson) creates attribution risk.
Measurement-error critiques may weaken the quantitative interpretation of the headline magnitudes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators are used in a vast amount of applied work across fields. They solved a genuine identification and estimation problem for dynamic relationships with individual effects, and the contribution is methodological infrastructure with very broad use.
assessment.attribution: Arellano–Bond (1991) is the core contribution, with Arellano–Bover and Blundell–Bond refining it. The three-person set is natural and the credit is fairly clear.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of use, so the impact is thoroughly established.
uncertainties: Proliferation of instruments and weak-instrument concerns in system GMM are known issues.
Methodological prizes are rarer than substantive ones, and the committee may judge the breakthrough narrower than the largest candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The law-and-finance program established that legal origins and investor protection systematically relate to financial development, and it opened a major empirical research agenda in comparative corporate finance and institutions. It is extremely highly cited and has had real policy influence.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer, and Vishny jointly wrote the foundational papers, so a three-name cap forces the omission of Vishny. Shleifer also has major separate contributions in behavioural finance and corporate governance.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty-five years of work. Maturity is high, but the empirical findings have been heavily criticised and revised.
uncertainties: Replication and identification concerns about the legal origins thesis, and about the data behind some indices, weigh against it.
The cap excludes Vishny, which is a meaningful attribution cost.
Shleifer's broader record may complicate how the committee frames the contribution.
